title: Go-live runway journal
content:
Purpose: personal running notes for the 2026-03-13 go-live. Use this as my quick checklist and comms scratchpad. Not the canonical runbook — copy into the official runbook after the cutover when I have time.

Top-level goals (quick):
- Push 3.14 config changes + small optimization hotfix (PR 4123)
- Backport security patch from main -> stable-3.14 for token caching edge case
- Keep latency SLOs within 95th <= 150ms on p50-pref workloads
- No customer-facing downtime; if we need to degrade, failover to 2.9-compatible variant and notify customers in #prod-ops

Timeline checkpoints (my local clock):
- 06:30 — wake/check Slack for overnight alerts (done)
- 07:15 — preflight: verify canary infra green (rolling metrics)
- 08:00 — notify SRE and oncall: start of cutover window (post template below)
- 09:00 — merge PR 4123, trigger CI (small)
- 09:30 — deploy to staging; run smoke tests (embedding + chat)
- 10:15 — start gradual rollout to hosted region us-west2 (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
- 11:45 — full rollout target; start post-rollout verification
- 12:30 — lunch unless rollback happens

Preflight quick checklist (things I actually check, in order):
- CI: all checks passed for PR 4123 and backport branch (green)
- Nightly alerts: no regressions in latency/CPU memory for last 12h
- Canaries: p95/latency <= 140ms; error rate < 0.03%
- Capacity: dedicated pool has 15% spare headroom; autoscaler healthy
- Secrets: KMS rotation note — confirm service token still valid (secret id svc/redwood-deploy-prod)
- Feature flags: ensure new routing flag is OFF by default and toggled manually during rollout

Backports to do (manual steps below):
- backport/security-cache-fix -> stable-3.14 (branch: backport/security-cache-fix-to-3.14)
  - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4142 (create if missing)
  - run unit + integ tests locally (script: ./scripts/test-backport.sh)
  - ping @Rosa for one quick review (she's on morning shift)

Commands I run often (copy these into terminal):
- Merge PR (local workflow): gh pr checkout 4123 && git rebase main && gh pr merge --squash
- Build image (CI override): make image TAG=3.14-hotfix && docker push registry.redwood.ai/platform:3.14-hotfix
- Trigger deploy: ./deploy/trigger.sh --env=prod --tag=3.14-hotfix --route=us-west2
- Rollback (fast): ./deploy/trigger.sh --env=prod --tag=3.13-stable --route=us-west2 && post in #prod-ops

Comms templates (Slack / Email) — use and tailor quickly:
- Slack to #prod-ops (start): "[GO-LIVE] Starting 3.14 rollout now — merging PR 4123, backport branch for security-cache-fix. Will do canary -> gradual. Monitoring p95/p50, post updates. Pager list OOO? @oncall please ack."
- Slack to #customer-notice (if degradation): "Heads up: we're seeing increased request latency for hosted-api in us-west2 after today's deploy. We're rolling back to 3.13 stable and will post ETA within 20m. Customers on dedicated instances unaffected. — Aisha"
- Email snippet for enterprise customers (if needed): "Subject: Planned update to Redwood Hosted API (3.14) — We are performing a rolling update aimed at improving cache stability. No downtime expected. We'll notify you immediately if action is required."

Smoke tests (quick personal checklist):
- basic generation: curl -X POST /v1/generate (sample prompt) -> 200, token stream ok
- chat session: start->continue->end, confirm KV cache reuse (logs show cache-hit events)
- embeddings: call embeddings endpoint with ~1k tokens payload, ensure latency < 250ms
- function-calling: run the example function call flow (edge case: missing args handling)

Rollforward / rollback decision tree (short):
- If errors spike > 0.5% or p95 > 250ms for > 10m -> pause rollout, rollback to 3.13
- If canary at 10% passes but 50% fails -> pause and investigate logs (kv-cache, OOM, oom-killer signals)
- If SLOs hold but specific customers report regressions -> temporary routing policy: route affected customers to variant:legacy-3.13 via routing flag and open customer ticket

Contacts (primary):
- SRE oncall: Ethan Kim (pager: +1-415-555-0183)
- Backup SRE: Marcus Li (slack: @marcus)
- Release reviewer: Rosa Martinez (Slack DM)
- PM (product): Jonah Reed (for client comms)

Outstanding/risks (my notes):
- We're still waiting on perf-profile numbers from the quantization change — if the real traffic distribution differs, p95 could move up (~10-15ms)
- One integration test flakes intermittently in CI (test_pipeline::embed-large) — plan: run 10x locally before merge
- Long tail error seen once in staging (HTTP 502 from envoy) — need to check upstream timeout config (envoy: 1.18 timeout default?)

Post-deploy tasks (quick):
- Collect traces for first 30m and upload to tracing-storage with tag release:3.14
- Run smoke runbook checklist and mark items in the canonical runbook
- Send post-deploy note to #prod-ops: "3.14 rolled out to us-west2 @ HH:MM — watch metrics; postmortem if any incident > sev2"
- If clean for 4h, update release notes and mark JIRA-RELEASE-842 as deployed

Personal TODO (what I need to do next):
- 07:45 — Rerun tests for backport branch (local)
- 08:50 — Post start comms in #prod-ops (copy template)
- 09:20 — Verify canary metrics after merge (p95/p50/err)
- 11:50 — Check customer routing flags status and confirm no stuck toggles
- After cutoff — draft short retrospective note about what clobbered the pipeline steps (if anything)

Notes to self (less formal):
- Remember: breathe. If rollback, don't try to patch quickly without a reproducer.
- Keep a screenshot of canary dashboard at each stage (timestamped) — helps postmortem.
- If Rosa is busy, ping Jonah to nudge SRE coverage.

Random scratch ideas (for future):
- Add a tiny synthetic load generator that mimics cache-heavy prefix behavior (would catch the token-cache edge case earlier)
- Consider adding a deploy tag visible in dashboard indicating "quantized" vs "non-quantized" variant for quicker attribution

End-of-day copy action: paste final timeline + key screenshots into Confluence page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/3.14-cutover-plan

-- Aisha (personal notes)
